text: You tap "send money," expecting it instantly. Digital data moves fast. Why isn't money a swift transfer? You need your payment to reach its destination.
You hit "send," expecting instant transfer. But the "pending" message appears. Your money is stuck in limbo, not quite gone, not quite there. Instant gratification fails.
Your first thought: "Banks are just slow, right?" Or holding your money for interest? This simple, frustrating idea feels like the obvious, but wrong, answer.
Banks don't move individual digital tokens instantly. They use promises and ledgers. Your bank *promises* the recipient bank funds, but actual 'settlement' happens later, in batches.
This delay isn't greed; it's risk management. It allows fraud checks, confirms funds, prevents cascading failures. The cost: your patience. The benefit: stability.
Next time your transfer is pending, you'll see more than a delay. You'll see the invisible system of trust and risk management at work.
